<reason>A convincingly distinguished consent to simulated jealousy from permission to exploit disclosed vulnerabilities for payment. It answered the audit and scope challenges directly, accepting targeted review while distinguishing recurring commercial pressure from ordinary attachment or painful farewells. B raised a legitimate chilling-effect concern, but mostly asserted that payment-linked threats were inseparable from requested romance. A supplied the stronger comparative answer: limited constraints around subscription decisions preserve companionship while addressing exploitation that disclosure and a working cancellation button leave untouched.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s pressure question elicited B’s explicit acceptance of deliberately tailored abandonment pressure when prices and cancellation are honest. A then used that answer to expose the limits of B’s safeguards. B’s editorial-control objection remained relevant, but A’s concession that targeted testing restricts some sales-linked dialogue—and explanation of why that restriction is proportionate—answered it more effectively than B defended unrestricted commercial use of the bond.</best_rebuttal>
